title: Tech Note: Developing with 4D Server Part 2: Setting Up a Multi-Developer Password System
author: Walt Nelson
featured_technology: 4D password system (Users & Groups, Design mode ownership/access)

historical_commentary.text: This is Part 2 of a three-part series on multi-developer 4D Server development, covering how to divide a project into functional modules and set up a binary Design Mode password system of Users and Groups so each module team owns its own Files, Forms, and Global Procedures. The overall discipline of dividing large projects into ownership-scoped modules with role-based access remains a sound software engineering practice, but the specific mechanics (Design Mode ownership of binary structure objects, single-Designer 4D Insider access, Global Procedures terminology) are dated relative to modern 4D, which introduced Project Mode (text-based, file-per-method source control friendly) in 2018 as an alternative that makes much of this binary-structure password juggling unnecessary.
related_updates: Design Mode is now called this because Project Mode was introduced in v17 (2018) as an alternative, text-based structure format that works naturally with modern source control (Git) branching/merging instead of binary-structure ownership locks

Modern multi-developer 4D teams commonly use Project Mode plus Git for concurrent development, reducing reliance on the Users/Groups Design-mode ownership scheme described here for source-level collaboration

"Global Procedures" terminology was later renamed to "Methods" starting with 4D V6 (the same 1997 release this note's series precedes), and 4D Insider's single-Designer-access limitation described here is a legacy constraint of binary structure files
